requirement: In Markdown, escaped roles and role-looking text in inline code, fenced code, or raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as references. Raw HTML means an HTML block, an HTML comment, or an inline HTML tag including its attributes; text between inline tags is ordinary Markdown. A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
rationale:
**Verdict: one gap, in the tests for fenced references inside raw HTML.**

**Implementation.** The behavior is reachable from the two `{impl}` items.
- `fenced::markdown_fences` (src/fenced.rs) takes `protected_ranges` (src/lib.rs). That function covers code blocks, inline code, HTML blocks and inline HTML tags, including their attributes. Fence lines that overlap those ranges are skipped. With `markdown=false` nothing is protected.
- `terms::direct_references` (src/terms.rs) reaches `referenced_terms`, then `reference_roles`, then `is_escaped` and `is_protected`.
  - `reference_roles` skips escaped roles, using the odd-backslash-count rule.
  - It also skips roles in code, HTML and HTML comments.
  - Inline HTML protects only the tag itself, so text between tags stays ordinary Markdown.
  - `direct_references` also calls `definition_blocks`, which uses `code_block_ranges` so that `:::{req}` inside a fenced code block does not define anything.
  - `definition_blocks` recognizes only colon-fence directives, and `reference_roles` has no `{req}` case. So a legacy inline `{req}` role defines nothing.
- This code is reached from the `{impl}` items, so it needs no references of its own.

**Tests that pass the obligations.**
- Escaped roles, including the double-backslash case: `markdown_examples_and_escaped_references_stay_literal`.
- Inline code and fenced code, across the `.md`, `.markdown`, `.MD` and `.Markdown` extensions, with plain text as the contrast: `every_markdown_extension_keeps_escaped_and_code_roles_literal`.
- Term roles: `term_dependencies_of_every_markdown_extension_skip_literal_roles` and `literal_term_roles_in_subject_and_requirements_inputs_need_no_definition`.
- Raw HTML for inline roles: `roles_in_raw_html_stay_literal` covers an HTML block, an HTML comment, an attribute value, and text between inline tags staying ordinary Markdown.
- `{req}` in a fenced code example and the legacy inline `{req}` role: `code_examples_and_legacy_roles_remain_literal` and `colon_directives_render_markdown_bodies_and_legacy_roles_stay_literal`.
- Role-looking text in code inside requirement bodies: `references_in_requirement_bodies_are_scanned_as_markdown`.

**Gap: no test covers fenced references in raw HTML.**
- The requirement says role-looking text in raw HTML MUST remain literal and MUST NOT count as a reference. A `:::{cite} name` fence is role-looking text.
- `markdown_fences` has its own branch for this. It marks a line as protected through `overlaps_protected` over HTML ranges, and `find_fences` then skips it. The doc comment says "fences in code or raw HTML remain literal".
- No test cited for this requirement puts a colon fence inside an HTML block, an HTML comment or an inline tag and asserts it is not a reference.
  - `every_markdown_extension_keeps_escaped_and_code_roles_literal` puts the fence only inside a ```` ```text ```` code block. Its HTML case is an attribute holding an inline role, not a fence.
  - `markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code` in src/fenced.rs also covers only code. It is cited for other requirements, not this one.
  - The HTML tests in src/lib.rs exercise only `reference_roles`.
- This obligation has a conditional and a transformation of its own, so the testing exemption does not apply. A test is needed that runs `markdown_fences` (or `text_references`) on a fence inside raw HTML and carries a `{test}` reference to `requirements.references.markdown_literals`.

No `{fixme}` acknowledges this gap, so it counts against the subject.

A `{req}` directive inside a fenced code example and a legacy inline `{req}` role MUST NOT define a requirement.
